headline: Singapore's president told the IMF and World Bank meetings that AI is already reducing demand for new graduates' first jobs and that governments should act soon.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: the Reuters text matches the headline, but it is a short report of a speech with no figures behind the claim.
importance_line: Fewer first jobs bears first on young people entering work, then on the governments and universities that prepare them, then on employers; it is a speaker's assertion at a meeting, and the report gives no numbers for the evidence he calls clear.
summary: Reuters reports that Tharman Shanmugaratnam, president of Singapore, told the annual gathering of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok on Monday 12 Oct that "the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand", that "the evidence is already very clear" and clearest in the most AI-exposed sectors, and that governments should address it "very soon". He also said the world should avoid a "new divergence" between developing and advanced economies because of AI disruption; Reuters gives no figures.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); read Reuters' text (reporting by Rae Wee) on Central Oregon Daily and The Economic Times; url kept as Reuters' own link. Same Bangkok meetings as the IMF chief's 'tsunami' warning (C05-01).
